newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel renews military pact with Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Israel renews military pact with Turkey.

text.p: Israel on Sunday said it had renewed a military cooperation pact with Turkey that has drawn the ire of Syria, Iran and Islamists.

"At the end of the week two days of talks in Turkey were concluded between Israel and Turkey," Israel's Defence Ministry said in a statement. "A strategic dialogue was held and an agreement was signed for cooperation and exercises for 1997."
It said the country teams were led by David Ivri, adviser to Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai, and Turkey's deputy army chief of staff.

In June, Islamist Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, who campaigned for election on a campaign pledge to scrap the deal with Israel, took office. He has since dropped attempts to act on the promise.
Turkish President Suleyman Demirel said in September that the defence and training pacts with the Jewish state would remain intact.

Israel and Turkey signed an agreement in February providing for, among other things, Israeli air force jets to train in Turkish air space. In August, the two states signed a defence industry cooperation deal.
Demirel said in September it was no secret the Israel-Turkey pact worried Iran and Syria but he said the accords were not directed against a third country.
